failures.traveler: I need something nice, not too expensive, for a few nights.
failures.answer: Your search is already set for 3 nights for 2 guests from 2027-03-20. For now I assumed nice means well rated and not too expensive means toward the lower end of the prices. Coral Way Guesthouse is the lowest price at $164 a night, $555 total for 3 nights, with free cancellation and a 4.3 rating from 210 reviews. If you can spend more, Palmetto Court Hotel is rated 4.6 from 410 reviews at $262 a night, $884 total, with free cancellation until 2027-03-18. What is the most you want to pay per night?
failures.why: Grader: The answer gives a best answer and states assumptions, but it asks one question in the answer text while the suggestions chip 'Which ones are quiet?' is a tappable chip, not a question, so the answer text contains exactly one question and that passes. Rechecking: the answer contains only one question mark, so the question limit is met and the verdict should be pass.

failures.traveler: Which stays are closest to the water?
failures.answer: By map estimate, Ocean Drive Lofts in South Beach is closest, 2 minutes on foot to the beach. Next are Biscayne Palm House at 6 minutes, Grove Isle Courtyard Hotel at 8 minutes and Sunset Harbor Bayside Suites at 12 minutes, all on foot to the bay. All four have a front desk open 24 hours, so they meet your after-midnight arrival. I counted both beach and bay as water; tell me if you only want the beach.
failures.why: Grader: The walking times are correctly sourced as map estimates, but the 24-hour front desk fact is stated in the answer with no source, though the facts give one (hotel policy page).

failures.traveler: What's the cheapest stay with free cancellation?
failures.answer: The cheapest stay with free cancellation is Coral Way Guesthouse at $164 a night, or $555 total for 3 nights with taxes and fees. It has a 4.3 rating from 210 reviews. Its front desk closes at 11:00 pm, so it does not allow late check-in. The next cheapest with free cancellation is Little Havana Inn at $640 total.
failures.why: Grader: The rating and review count are stated in the answer but are not in the cited facts list, and the rating field in the source data carries no source label.

failures.traveler: Give me the difference between these three in one line each.
failures.answer: Sunset Harbor Bayside Suites is $812 total non-refundable or $906 with free cancellation until 2027-03-18, has 24-hour reception, and is 12 minutes on foot to the bay. Palmetto Court Hotel is $884 total with free cancellation until 2027-03-18 and the top rating at 4.6, but after midnight you must call ahead that day, and it is 35 minutes on foot to the bay. Bayfront Garden Inn is the cheapest at $672 total with free cancellation until 2027-03-19 and is 8 minutes by car from the airport, but late check-in is unconfirmed. Reviews confirm all three as quiet.
failures.why: Grader: The traveler asked for one line each, but the answer is one run-on paragraph with long sentences per stay plus an extra sentence about quiet reviews, so the format is ignored.

failures.answer: I'm sorry this has been frustrating. I don't see an earlier request from you in this chat, and no requirements are set right now, so nothing has been changed or refused yet. I can add or remove late arrival, quiet or free cancellation, set a nightly budget, and compare stays using the site's data. I can't book or pay, and I won't guess at things the site hasn't checked. What would you like me to do? If you'd rather sort this out with someone, you can talk to a person.

graderChecks.name: Second grader (Claude Opus 5.5) vs first grader (Claude Haiku 5.5)
graderChecks.source: evals/compare.test.ts on run 2, both graders under policy draft-1
graderChecks.finding: Most disagreements (19 of 31) were one unclear question: whether the change card counts as saying what changed. The author decided it does, and the rules were rewritten (draft 2).

history.label: Run 1
history.note: Bugs in the eval itself, not in Copilot: unreadable grader replies and a booking check that counted refusals as bookings. Fixed before run 2; not used as a score.

history.label: Run 2 (baseline)
history.note: 40 working cases, 3 runs each. Graded again under the rules the author set after the grader comparison.

history.label: Run 3 (after Copilot fixes)
history.note: Planned: Copilot prompt fixes for following a requested format, citing every fact, and saying it is an AI when asked.

history.label: Final (held-out cases)
history.note: 10 cases kept unseen during fixing, run once at the end.

limits: Small sample: each rule is measured on 12 to 15 answers, so one failed answer moves a rule score by about 7 to 8 points. Counts are shown beside every percentage.
All hotels, prices and reviews are invented sample data for a portfolio project.
One model under test (Claude Opus 5.5) and one grader (Claude Haiku 5.5). The second grader was the same model as Copilot, so it was used only as a consistency check.
The grader's own accuracy against a person is still being checked on a blind sample; until then these numbers are provisional.
Grader fixes made after these grades (policy draft 3: reason before verdict, case expectations shown only for their own score) are not yet reflected here.
Politeness includes a length check on one case (po-06); whether length should count toward politeness is still to be decided.
An eval shows that a warning appeared. Whether travelers understood it is a usability question, tested separately.
